clue.text: Russia's leader and top player switched in first half

indicators.note: the two letters making up the front half of the word are swapped round

parts.note: a top player in any field is a star

explanation.surface: A Russian sports team's captain swaps places with its best player before half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched in first half' swaps the first two letters of STAR, ST becoming TS, while AR stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor and supreme ruler of Russia before the revolution.

clue.text: Put out grant for part of US city

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: to grant a point is to own or admit it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to issue a grant for a district of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT into UPT; OWN is grant in the sense of conceding something is true.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the uptown area is the residential or upper district of a city, away from downtown.

clue.text: Person swearing disturbed lamb, sheep and ram, initially

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of their order and set down afresh
initially takes only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone curses a startled flock of lamb, sheep and ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from ram; 'disturbed' then rearranges LAMB, SHEEP and R together.
explanation.definitionFit: A blasphemer is one who speaks profanely, and swearing is profane speech.

clue.text: Hits hard in part of UK

indicators.note: in places the letter for hard inside the name of the country

parts.note: Wales is one of the four countries of the United Kingdom
H is the standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone lands heavy blows somewhere in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits hard' looks like one phrase, but hard is the H. 'in' puts H inside WALES.
explanation.definitionFit: To whale someone is an informal verb meaning to beat or thrash them, so whales means hits.

clue.text: Visibly embarrassed about condition, in other words

indicators.note: about means the colour word goes round the word for condition

parts.note: someone visibly embarrassed has gone red in the face
a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: Someone blushes when their condition is put to them in plain terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restated has been said again, typically expressed using different wording.

clue.text: Animals in tall grass rearing up

indicators.note: in a down clue rearing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses growing in wet places

explanation.surface: Animals stand among the tall grass, rising up on their hind legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer are hoofed ruminant animals, the stags bearing antlers.

clue.text: Construction in Dublin I demolished? Good

indicators.note: a demolished thing is broken up, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether knocking down a building in Dublin would be good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges DUBLIN and I into BUILDIN, then G for good finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A building is a structure that has been constructed, so it is a construction.

clue.text: Drink a lot of 16, say

definitions.meaning: a colloquial shortening of beverage, a drink
16 is larks, and a ... is a collective name for a flock of larks

explanation.walkthrough: The '16' points to the answer at 16-down, as in this theme's other collective-noun clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevy is slang for an alcoholic drink and also a flock or company of birds such as larks or quails.

clue.text: Hercule P's mistaken where body is found

indicators.note: mistaken letters are wrongly placed, so they must be put in a different order

parts.note: the name and initial with its S, the fictional Belgian detective Hercule Poirot shortened

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's detective gets it wrong about where the corpse lies.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive is needed here: 'mistaken' rearranges all of HERCULEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a tomb, the place where a dead body is laid to rest.

clue.text: Duet arranged before or after English piece of music

indicators.note: the new letters may stand on either side of E, both orders giving the same word
arranged is the musician's word for reworking, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A duet is arranged before or after an English composition.
explanation.walkthrough: Both orders work, E then the rest or the rest then E, so 'before or after' is literally true rather than padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a short musical composition written as a study to practise a technique.

clue.text: Cheats those assembled in 7

definitions.meaning: to cheat someone is to rook them, swindle them
7 is building, and a building of birds of this black crow family is their collective name

explanation.walkthrough: '7' is BUILDING at 7-down, a collective noun for these birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rook means swindle as a verb, and rooks are colonial crows whose gathering is called a building.

clue.text: It's what could snatch victory from one side

definitions.meaning: a late comeback in a match, read as two words
sideways, from the side

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LATE RALLY for the first sense: a comeback near the end of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways or from the side, while late rally is a comeback that can win a match.

clue.text: Performs slow movement with female singers

parts.note: to inch is to move slowly, little by little

explanation.surface: Women vocalists edge slowly across the stage during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performs slow movement' sounds musical, but means creeps along.
explanation.definitionFit: Finches are small songbirds, so they are singers in the natural sense.

clue.text: Piece of information about European side

indicators.note: about here means the information word wraps round the European letter

parts.note: a fact is a single piece of information

explanation.surface: A snippet of news concerns the European side of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one aspect or side of something, like a face of a cut gem.

clue.text: Police statement detailing charge put on table

definitions.meaning: British slang for the police force, often prefixed with old

definitions.text: statement detailing charge put on table
definitions.meaning: a restaurant bill, an account of what is owed, laid on the table

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a police charge sheet; the second sense is the restaurant bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bill is British slang for the police, and the bill is the statement of what a diner owes.

clue.text: Rapture at being accepted by Texan oil organisation

indicators.note: being accepted by puts the little word inside the reordered letters
organisation means the letters are organised into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone is ecstatic at joining a Texas oil company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Texan oil organisation' reads as an oil company, but organisation is the anagram signal working on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaltation is a feeling of intense joy or elation, close in sense to rapture.

clue.text: Jokes collected together in 15

definitions.meaning: pranks or bits of fun
15 is exaltation, the collective name for a flock of these songbirds

explanation.walkthrough: '15' refers to EXALTATION at 15-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks means pranks or escapades, and also songbirds gathered in an exaltation.

clue.text: Attraction of 13 across

definitions.meaning: an appealing quality, allure
13 across is finches, and their flock has this collective name

explanation.walkthrough: '13 across' refers to FINCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm means attractiveness, and a charm of finches is the collective noun for those birds.

clue.text: A request for help about top cause of respiratory disease

indicators.note: about means the distress call goes round the word for top

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal asking for help

explanation.surface: Someone sends a distress call about the main cause of lung illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos fibres, when inhaled, cause lung diseases such as asbestosis and mesothelioma.

clue.text: Seed vessel that contains 4

definitions.meaning: the casing holding peas or beans
4 is whales, and a group of them is called by this collective name

explanation.walkthrough: '4' refers to WHALES at 4-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a seed case, as for peas, and also a school of whales or dolphins.

clue.text: Act badly as lawyer and corruptly get profit without right

indicators.note: corruptly suggests the letters are corrupted into a different order
without means the letter for right is dropped from the mix

explanation.surface: A dishonest lawyer makes money crookedly, with no regard for what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes R from GET PROFIT, and 'corruptly' rearranges the remaining GETPOFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pettifog is to practise as a petty, quibbling or unscrupulous lawyer.

clue.text: Annoyance concealed by German repeatedly

indicators.note: concealed by says the answer lies inside that doubled string, the outer letters stripped away
repeatedly means the nationality word is written out twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written, the nationality word

explanation.surface: A man's irritation is kept hidden by a German, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Write German twice, GERMANGERMAN; 'concealed by' strips GERM from the front and MAN from the end, leaving the run across the join: germ-AN GER-man.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is strong annoyance or displeasure.

clue.text: Tasteless stuff covering plain fabric

indicators.note: covering means the junk word wraps round the plain word

parts.note: tat is tasteless, cheap tawdry goods

explanation.surface: Gaudy trimmings cover a plain cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods. Tabaret is an upholstery fabric with satin stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a durable silk furnishing fabric with alternating satin and watered stripes.

clue.text: Alternative to lighter copies

definitions.meaning: things struck to make a flame instead of using a cigarette lighter
duplicates or equals, things that correspond

explanation.definitionFit: Matches are small sticks struck to make fire, and also counterparts that correspond exactly.

clue.text: 28 collectively commit serious crime

definitions.meaning: 28 is crows, and their gathering has this grim collective name
to kill someone unlawfully

explanation.walkthrough: '28' refers to CROWS at 28-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A murder of crows is the collective noun, and to murder is to commit homicide.

clue.text: Relentlessly pursues those in 24 down

definitions.meaning: to dog or chase someone without let-up
24 down is pack, and hunting dogs gather in one

explanation.walkthrough: '24 down' refers to PACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound is to harass persistently, and hounds are hunting dogs that run in a pack.

clue.text: Silly tries let in by inadequate back

indicators.note: let in by places the jumbled letters inside the word for inadequate

parts.note: poor means inadequate, not good enough

indicators.note: silly means the letters are jumbled in a foolish order

explanation.surface: Feeble defending lets the opposition score silly tries from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby surface makes 'back' look like a player position, but it is the definition, as in rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior means situated at the back, rear rather than front.

clue.text: Some rugby players prepare to go on tour

definitions.meaning: the forwards in a rugby team, who form the scrum
put clothes into a suitcase before travelling

explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the pack is the forwards collectively, and to pack is to fill a case for a trip.

clue.text: Take part in bridge as this, never meeting partner?

indicators.note: Take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bridge player who never gets to sit with their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote that East and West shall never meet; at the bridge table the same seat partners West, so the surface also works as a partial &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's Ballad of East and West opens with the line that the two compass points never meet.

clue.text: Trace, contact and meet

definitions.meaning: a slight amount, a hint
physical contact or being in communication
to come together, as lines that meet at a point

explanation.definitionFit: Touch can mean a small trace, physical contact or communication, and to adjoin or meet.

clue.text: Group of 6, perhaps, coming from another direction

indicators.note: coming from says the letters are drawn out of the words next to it

explanation.surface: A party of six people approaches from somewhere unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles anot-HER D-irection. '6' refers to DEER at 6-down, whose group has this collective name.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a group of animals such as deer or cattle that live or move together.

clue.text: King surrounded by 27, perhaps, is triumphant

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the royal letter inside the animals word

parts.note: 27 is herd, and cows are one example of what forms a herd
R is the abbreviation for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: A king hemmed in by a herd somehow still comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: '27, perhaps' refers to HERD at 27-down, which cows are an example of.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to exult or boast loudly over a victory.

clue.text: Ponder o'er strange formation of spaced-out men

indicators.note: strange signals an odd, unusual arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A soldier contemplates a peculiar military drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the nine letters of PONDER O'ER, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Open order is a military formation in which troops are spread out with wide intervals.
